tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: A tennis ball hits the floor with a speed $v$ at an angle $\theta$ with the normal to the floor. If the collision is inelastic and the co-efficient of restitution is $\varepsilon$, what will be the angle of reflection?

solution.text:
Hint:
$\tan \theta^{\prime}=\frac{\operatorname{usin} \theta}{\operatorname{eucos} \theta} \quad \tan \theta^{\prime}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}} \tan \theta$ Since the floor is smooth. Hence tangential component of velocity remains unchanged.
